examples.en: That singer's high notes are powerful and clear.

examples.ko: 고음을 낼 때 목이 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: Your throat can hurt when you hit high notes.
The high-note part of this song is hard.
The sound got thinner as it went higher.
I am worried my voice will crack on the high notes.

examples.ko: 저는 고음은 잘 못 내지만 저음은 자신 있어요.
examples.en: I cannot hit high notes well, but I am confident with low ones.

explain: '저음'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 노래방에서는 높은 음을 못 내는 사람이 '고음 불가'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: That singer hits high notes well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 소리를 목으로 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for producing a high note with one's voice.

phrases.en: I have a cold, so I can't reach the high notes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 소리를 내지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you cannot produce high notes.

phrases.en: At karaoke, I can't sing high notes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농담처럼 가볍게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light, joking expression.

explain_en: It pairs with 저음. At karaoke, people who cannot reach high notes sometimes joke '고음 불가'.

examples.en: I stopped walking in front of the cliff.
The side of the road was a steep drop, so I was scared.
I had a dream of falling off a cliff.
Please don't go toward the cliff edge.
There are many steep drops on the mountain trail, so be careful.
You can see the sea below the cliff.

explain: '절벽'은 높고 가파른 바위 벽 자체를 말하고, '낭떠러지'는 그 끝에서 아래로 떨어지는 위험한 곳을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다', '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'처럼 써요. 위험한 상황을 비유할 때도 나와요.

phrases.en: In the movie, a car fell off a cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳에서 아래로 떨어지는 위험한 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dangerous situation of falling from a high place.

phrases.en: Please don't go to the edge of the cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 가장자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about the dangerous edge.

phrases.en: There is a high cliff by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바위 벽 자체를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for the rock wall itself.

explain_en: '절벽' is the steep rock wall itself, while '낭떠러지' feels natural when you mean the dangerous drop at the edge. You say '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다' or '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'. It can also be used figuratively for a dangerous situation.

examples.en: I record my favorite drama.
I recorded the class and watched it again later.
I recorded the game, but there's no sound.
Please be quiet while we're recording.

examples.ko: 방송을 녹화하려면 먼저 저장 공간을 확인하세요.
examples.en: If you want to record a broadcast, check the storage space first.
May I record the presentation?

explain: 녹화하다는 영상을 기록해 두는 거예요. 소리만 기록하는 것은 '녹음하다'예요. '생방송'과 반대로, 미리 녹화한 방송은 '녹화 방송'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This program is a recorded broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생방송과 반대로, 미리 찍은 방송을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of a live broadcast; a pre-recorded show.

phrases.en: I'll record the game and keep it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'로 나중에 보려고 미리 해 놓는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아/어 두다 means doing it in advance for later.

phrases.en: When the camera turns on, recording starts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상을 찍기 시작할 때 '녹화'와 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 녹화 when video recording begins.

explain_en: 녹화하다 is to record video. Recording sound only is '녹음하다', so keep them apart. In contrast to a '생방송' (live broadcast), a pre-recorded program is a '녹화 방송'.

examples.en: The motor of this fan is broken.
At night the motor sound is too loud.
We attached a small motor to the boat.
The repairman replaced the motor with a new one.
There is a motor inside a washing machine.
Electric cars run on a motor instead of an engine.

explain: 전기로 돌아가는 장치는 '모터', 기름을 태워 움직이는 장치는 '엔진'이에요. 전동 킥보드와 전기 자전거는 모터, 오토바이는 엔진이에요. '전동기'라는 한자어도 있지만 일상에서는 '모터'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '모터가 돌다', '모터가 고장 나다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: This bike has an electric motor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기로 움직이는 모터라는 것을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is an electric motor.

phrases.en: The fan's motor doesn't turn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모터가 작동하지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a motor does not run.

phrases.en: I like it because the motor sound is quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 돌아갈 때 나는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound a machine makes while running.

explain_en: A device spun by electricity is a 'motor', while one that burns fuel is an 'engine' (엔진). Electric scooters and e-bikes have motors, while motorcycles have engines. There is also the Sino-Korean word '전동기', but in daily life '모터' is used far more. It pairs with '모터가 돌다' (the motor spins) and '모터가 고장 나다' (the motor breaks).

examples.ko: 주문한 음식이 삼십 분 만에 배달됐어요.
examples.en: The food I ordered was delivered in thirty minutes.
This book will be delivered tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 우유가 매일 집 앞으로 배달되어서 편해요.
examples.en: Milk is delivered to my door every day, which is convenient.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 택배가 늦게 배달될 거예요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the parcel will be delivered late.
The packaging got a bit damaged while it was being delivered.
It was delivered to the wrong address, so I received it again.

explain: '배달하다'는 가져다주는 사람이 주어이고, '배달되다'는 물건이 주어예요. '피자가 배달됐어요'처럼 물건 쪽에서 말해요. 음식은 '배달', 쇼핑 상자는 '택배'라고 많이 부르고, '택배 왔어요'처럼 '오다'로 가볍게 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A package is coming this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑 상자가 집에 도착하는 것을 '오다'로 가볍게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to say a shopping parcel arrives at home, using 'come'.

phrases.en: This store delivers to your home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가져다주는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person bringing the item is the subject.

phrases.en: The delivery is late because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 늦게 올 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when food arrives late.

explain_en: With 배달하다 the person bringing it is the subject; with 배달되다 the item is the subject, as in 'the pizza got delivered'. Food is usually called 배달 and shopping boxes 택배, and 택배 is often said casually with 오다, as in 택배 왔어요.

p.n: 배달되다 means a courier brought it to the address. 전달되다 means it was passed along from person to person.

en: to be uneasy; to be anxious

examples.en: The child's expression looks uneasy.
I waited for the result with an uneasy heart.
He looked at the door uneasily.
The child walking alone looked uneasy.
His voice sounded uneasy, so I was worried.
If you look uneasy, I'll help you.

explain: '불안스럽다'는 겉으로 불안해 보이는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 내 기분을 말할 때는 '불안하다'를 더 자주 써요. '불안스러워 보이다'처럼 다른 사람을 보고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: My friend looks a bit uneasy today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 보고 느낌을 말할 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most natural when describing how another person looks.

phrases.en: The child is standing with an anxious look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun.

phrases.en: I always feel anxious before exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 기분을 말할 때는 '불안하다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For your own feelings, '불안하다' is used more often.

explain_en: 불안스럽다 describes a look or manner that appears anxious from outside. For your own feeling, 불안하다 is used more often. It is commonly used when watching someone else, as in '불안스러워 보이다' (look uneasy).

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 매주 금요일 밤에 생방송해요.
examples.en: This program airs live every Friday night.
I heard they'll broadcast the prime minister's announcement live this evening.

examples.ko: 생방송하는 중에는 실수해도 다시 찍을 수 없어서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: During a live broadcast you can't redo a mistake, so I get nervous.
The singer broadcast the fan meeting live.
I wish they would broadcast the game live from start to finish.
The sound cut out while they were broadcasting the concert live yesterday.

explain: 보통은 '생방송'이라는 명사로 많이 말해서 '생방송으로 나와요', '생방송 중이에요'처럼 써요. 행사나 경기를 그대로 보여 줄 때는 '생중계하다'도 자주 써요. 반대는 미리 찍어 두는 '녹화방송'이에요.

phrases.en: Today's game is shown live.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여서 방송이 나오는 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-으로' to say the way the broadcast is shown.

phrases.example: 지금 생방송 중이니까 조용히 해 주세요.
phrases.en: We're live right now, so please be quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이 지금 진행되고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the broadcast is happening right now.

phrases.en: The broadcaster airs the World Cup game live.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 경기를 현장에서 바로 보여 줄 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More often used for showing an event or game live from the scene.

explain_en: People more often use the noun '생방송', as in '생방송으로 나와요' or '생방송 중이에요'. For showing an event or game as it happens, '생중계하다' is also common. The opposite is '녹화방송', which is recorded in advance.

examples.en: The broken bike has been repaired.
The computer gets repaired within two days.
I picked up the repaired phone today.

examples.ko: 오래된 다리가 수리되는 동안 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: While the old bridge is being repaired, the road is blocked.
I'll contact you as soon as it's repaired.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 수리되지 않아서 앉으면 위험해요.
examples.en: This chair hasn't been repaired, so it's dangerous to sit on.

explain: 고치는 사람이 주어이면 '수리하다', 고장 난 물건이 주어이면 '수리되다'예요. '고치다'는 습관이나 버릇에도 쓰지만 '수리하다'는 기계, 건물, 도로 같은 물건에만 써요.

phrases.en: The phone will be repaired tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 고쳐질 일을 말해요. 서비스센터 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes something that will be fixed in the future. You often hear it at service centers.

phrases.en: The air conditioner hasn't been repaired yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고장 난 물건이 아직 고쳐지지 않았다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It says the broken item has not been fixed yet.

phrases.en: The broken chair got fixed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수리되다'보다 쉽고 일상적이에요. 물건이 고쳐진 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is simpler and more everyday than '수리되다'. It states the result of something being fixed.

explain_en: When the repairer is the subject use '수리하다'; when the broken item is the subject use '수리되다'. '고치다' can also be used for habits, but '수리하다' is only for things like machines, buildings, and roads.

examples.en: My uncle is getting married next month.

examples.ko: 아들이 장가갈 나이가 됐는데 연애도 안 해요.
examples.en: My son is of marrying age, but he isn't even dating.
I was the MC on the day my friend got married.

examples.ko: 형은 작년에 장가가서 지금 신혼집에 살아요.
examples.en: My older brother got married last year and now lives in their newlywed home.
I'm going to save money before I get married.
After getting married, I felt more responsible.

explain: 남자가 결혼한다는 뜻으로만 써요. 여자가 결혼할 때는 '시집가다'라고 했지만, 요즘은 남녀 모두 '결혼하다'가 가장 무난해요. 어른들이 농담처럼 '장가 언제 가니?'라고 묻기도 해요.

phrases.en: My older brother will get married next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미래의 결혼 계획을 말하는 활용형이에요. 남자에게만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a future form for marriage plans. Use it only for men.

phrases.en: My uncle still hasn't gotten married.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼하지 못한 남자를 말할 때 써요. 듣는 사람에 따라 실례일 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a man who hasn't married. It can be rude depending on who hears it.

phrases.en: My older brother is getting married next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남녀 모두에게 쓰는 가장 무난한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the safest word, and it works for both men and women.

explain_en: It is used only for a man marrying. For a woman the old word is '시집가다', but today '결혼하다' is the safest for everyone. Elders sometimes ask jokingly, '장가 언제 가니?' (When are you getting married?).

examples.en: The application will be processed by the end of today.

examples.ko: 그 문제가 아주 빠르게 처리돼서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm glad the problem was handled quickly.
How is this trash disposed of?
The refund hasn't been processed yet.
Because everything was handled at once, mistakes happened.

examples.ko: 주문이 처리되고 나면 알림이 올 거예요.
examples.en: You'll get a notification once the order is processed.

explain: 일, 서류, 문제가 절차대로 다뤄질 때 써요. 회사, 은행, 관공서에서 자주 들어요. '해결되다'는 문제가 풀린 결과를, '처리되다'는 일이 다뤄지는 과정을 말할 때 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: The problem was solved this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처리되다'는 일이 다뤄지는 과정이고, '해결되다'는 문제가 풀린 결과예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '처리되다' is about the process of handling; '해결되다' is about the problem being solved.

phrases.en: The documents are handled faster than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빨리'와 함께 일이 빠르게 진행된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '빨리', it means the matter moves along quickly.

phrases.en: Your application is being processed now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 진행 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means it is in progress right now.

explain_en: It is used when a task, document, or problem is dealt with step by step, and you hear it often at companies, banks, and government offices. 해결되다 focuses on the problem being solved, while 처리되다 focuses on the process of handling it.

en: to be treated; to be cured; to recover

examples.ko: 이 병은 일찍 발견하면 치료될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This illness can be treated if it is found early.
My injured leg was treated well at the hospital.

examples.ko: 치아가 완전히 치료되려면 세 번 더 와야 해요.
examples.en: For the tooth to be fully treated, you need to come three more times.

examples.ko: 치료되는 동안에는 무리한 운동을 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't overexercise while you are being treated.

examples.ko: 많이 아팠지만 지금은 다 치료돼서 괜찮아요.
examples.en: I was very sick, but now I'm fully treated and fine.

examples.ko: 상처가 치료되고 나면 흉터가 거의 안 남아요.
examples.en: Once the wound is treated, hardly any scar remains.

explain: '감기가 낫다'처럼 일상에서 병이 좋아질 때는 '낫다'가 더 자연스러워요. '치료되다'는 병원이나 치료를 거쳐 나을 때 쓰는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 내가 치료받는 건 '치료를 받다', 의사가 하는 건 '치료하다'예요.

phrases.example: 약을 먹고 며칠 지나면 나을 거예요.
phrases.en: You'll get better after a few days of taking medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 병이 좋아질 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural everyday word for getting better from an illness.

phrases.example: 이 병은 약으로 치료될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This illness can be treated with medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다'를 붙여 나을 가능성이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다', it means there's a chance of recovery.

phrases.example: 치료가 잘 돼서 이제 안 아파요.
phrases.en: The treatment went well, so it doesn't hurt anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치료되다'를 풀어 쓴 모양으로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out form of '치료되다' that is common in speech.

explain_en: In everyday talk, 낫다 is more natural for getting over a cold. 치료되다 is a slightly formal word for recovering through hospital care or treatment. You say 치료를 받다 when you receive treatment and 치료하다 for what the doctor does.

dis.h: an illness is cured by medical care

p.n: 치유되다 stresses full healing, also for emotions.
